learning_outcomes.text: Explains the basic principles of refrigeration, refrigeration cycles, and the operating principles of refrigeration systems.
Explains the functions and operating principles of compressors, condensers, evaporators, and expansion devices used in refrigeration systems.
Analyzes the vapor-compression refrigeration cycle thermodynamically and calculates the basic performance parameters of the cycle.
Evaluates refrigerants and refrigerant selection criteria used in refrigeration systems and compares the energy efficiency and performance of different systems.
Selects an appropriate refrigeration system for different applications and performs basic design and performance calculations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to refrigeration, basic concepts, history, and engineering applications of refrigeration
Thermodynamic fundamentals of refrigeration, heat transfer, and the refrigeration principle
Refrigeration cycles and classification of refrigeration systems
Vapor-compression refrigeration cycle and its operating principle
Compressors: types, construction, operating principles, and selection criteria
Condensers: types, construction, operating principles, and heat transfer
Evaporators: types, construction, operating principles, and heat transfer
Expansion devices: capillary tubes, thermostatic expansion valves, and electronic expansion valves
Refrigerants: properties, classification, selection criteria, and environmental impacts
Thermodynamic analysis of the vapor-compression refrigeration cycle and p-h/T-s diagrams
Refrigeration capacity, compressor power, COP, and energy efficiency calculations
Selection of refrigeration systems, basic principles of system design, and capacity calculations
Applications of refrigeration systems: commercial, industrial, air-conditioning, and food refrigeration systems
Energy efficiency in refrigeration systems, performance evaluation, and example system design
